subject: Request: Provisional IRP extract & SIG evidence for upcoming audit — customer notification plan
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintegrity.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: security@fintegrity.com
Date: 2025-05-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: provisional IRP extract + SIG evidence for May audit

Hi Aditya,

We're working on the SIG submission for our upcoming customer audit next week and the audit team asked for a provisional copy of Redwood's Incident Response Plan and a small set of supporting artifacts they can review ahead of the call. Specifically they requested: IRP extract (process overview, escalation matrix), recent post-incident timeline (redacted if needed), and sample telemetry extracts showing alerting.

Can you confirm whether you can provide: 1) an IRP extract (PDF), 2) an index mapping SIG controls to evidence files, and 3) a short statement on customer notification policy? They asked for initial materials by EOD tomorrow (2025-05-14).

If there are any concerns about sharing the telemetry export directly, we can do a sanitized export or provide screenshots. Let me know who on your side I should loop in.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Security Manager, Fintegrity

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintegrity.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: provisional IRP extract + SIG evidence for May audit

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up. Happy to help. Laura and Neha from security/compliance are cc'd; we own the IRP and evidence pack. Quick answers: we can provide a provisional IRP extract and a SIG evidence index by tomorrow EOD. Telemetry: we will provide a sanitized CSV extract (no PII), plus a short readme describing sampling.

One ask: do you need us to include the full escalation contact details (phone numbers)? We typically redact direct phone numbers for third-party audits and provide role-based contacts instead.

I will assemble an initial bundle and share a Drive link. Also planning to draft a short customer notification blurb in case the auditors request proof of customer-facing communication policy.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Lead — Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintegrity.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-14T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: provisional IRP extract + SIG evidence for May audit

Alex / team —

Attached: IRP_v2.1.pdf (provisional extract, redacted escalation details), sig_evidence_index.xlsx (matrix linking SIG control IDs to artifacts), and telemetry_export_20250512.csv (sanitized sample).

Notes:
- Phone numbers redacted; replaced with role-based contacts (Security Ops, Legal, Customer Success).
- Telemetry is for a 24-hour window around the May 12 alert; we removed client-identifiable strings.
- We've flagged two items in the index as "customer-notify" to demonstrate our notification policy: section 4.2 in the IRP describes timeline and thresholds.

If the auditors want unredacted escalation contacts we need an explicit NDA + written justification; please let us know.

Attachments: IRP_v2.1.pdf (provisional), sig_evidence_index.xlsx, telemetry_export_20250512.csv

—Laura Bennett
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: audits@crowne-sys.com <audits@crowne-sys.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintegrity.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: provisional IRP extract + SIG evidence for May audit

Laura / Aditya —

Received the bundle, thanks. Quick clarifying question on the notification workflow: in IRP v2.1 section 4.2 you reference a 72-hour customer notification window for incidents that materially affect data confidentiality. Can you confirm whether that is a hard SLA or a target? Also, please provide a sanitized example of a customer notification message (we'd like to see tone and timing).

If you can provide that by Friday morning (2025-05-16 09:00 PT) it will help us finalize the SIG map.

Regards,
Crowne Systems Audit Team

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: audits@crowne-sys.com <audits@crowne-sys.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: provisional IRP extract + SIG evidence for May audit

Hi —

Thanks for the question. Section 4.2 reflects our standard policy: customer notification is an SLA-level commitment for incidents that meet the materiality threshold defined in the IRP (data exposure or sustained availability degradation). Practically we treat 72 hours as a target SLA; exceptions are documented with the incident record and require VP-level sign-off.

Attached is a sanitized example notification draft we send to customers when an incident meets the threshold — file: redacted_postmortem_v1.txt (this is a template with placeholders, no customer identifiers). The template includes: scope summary, impact assessment, mitigations, next steps, and a contact for ongoing updates.

If Crowne needs a version with explicit escalation times (owner names/phone numbers) for audit purposes we can provide that under an NDA; otherwise the role-based version should suffice.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: IRP_v2.1.pdf (application/pdf), sig_evidence_index.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), telemetry_export_20250512.csv (text/csv), redacted_postmortem_v1.txt (text/plain)
